note: Small primitive campground on the North Fork of the White River: a gravel spur road on the wooded bench north of the river with about eight short back-in gravel pads and a privy at the turnaround loop. The river is 45-60 m south through a belt of timber, reached on foot; the canoe launch and Althea Spring are on the other side of Route H. The pads look 10-12 m long on imagery; spot length is not published. Route H crosses the river on a narrow one-lane bridge just south of the entrance; arriving from the north avoids it. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Individual Campsites' - one GIS camping point and a Camping Area symbol on the 2026 map, on a gravel camp road with ~8 gravel pads and a privy. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Not waterfront kept (timber belt to the river). Pin on the pads. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION (stays): the area page lists 'Camping: Individual Campsites' and says 'Parking, privies, campsites, a gravel canoe launch ramp and a .3 mile Althea Spring Trail'. The map (last updated 7/22/2026) draws a Camping Area symbol on the spur road east of the first parking lot, with privies at both ends; GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point (OBJECTID 30) = the stored pin. On the 0.24 m/px leaf-off frame the spur is a gravel road ~330 m long ending in a turnaround loop with a privy, with about eight short gravel back-in spurs (roughly 10-12 m each) on both sides of it - a real small campground, not a lot. A 23-ft rig fits the pads as seen; no length is published.

ACCESS: no ford. Route H crosses the North Fork ~350 m south-west of the camp on a narrow one-lane concrete bridge (Patrick Bridge, ~60 m long, seen on imagery; no weight or width posting found - the Overpass mirror did not answer, so OSM tags are unread). The entrance is on the north bank, so a rig arriving from the north (Route H from KK/PP) does not cross it; MDC's directions from Caulfield (US 160, then H north 4 miles) do. Caveat written in the note. No 4WD wording on the page.

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront, kept): the pads sit on a wooded bench; the nearest (south-side) spurs are ~45 m from the river bank with continuous hardwood timber between and no open apron; the river is ~40 m wide here. No official campsite photo shows the river from a pad.
PIN: stored 36.64361,-92.22116 = GIS point 30, on the row of pads north of the camp road - fine.

Area size: the page's Quick Facts say 170.7 acres, its text and the map 161 acres.
Season (manual, year-round) left as stored; no brochure is published for this area.
